title: Both stale-bounce pins can never exercise the typed-compare gate — the email-only fixtures are excluded before the gate runs
evidence:
+  // The pre-correction send: delivered entry an hour ago (now()-relative —
+  // r3 N10: an absolute fixture is clock-dependent).
+  let assert Ok(_) =
+    pog.query(
+      "UPDATE reference_call
+       SET attempts = jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object('at', to_char(now() - interval '1 hour', 'YYYY-MM-DD\"T\"HH24:MI:SS\"Z\"'), 'channel', 'email', 'outcome', 'delivered', 'detail', 'old_send_1')),
+           status = 'awaiting_correction'::reference_call_status
+       WHERE id = $1::uuid",
+    )
+  row_field(db, call_id, "status") |> should.equal(Some("queued"))
detail: Both fixtures write a single email entry with no same-timestamp sms sibling, so the find's email-without-sms exclusion drops the row before matched_send_at/send_is_post_correction are evaluated. Reverting the r2 typed compare to the r1 string compare would not fail either test — the gate's stale branch is unpinned.
recommended_fix: Add a stale fixture with email+sms entries at the same at so the send-ref leg matches, and assert stand-down flows through the typed compare; keep the email-only cases as not-found pins.

title: The sweep-exclusion and taken-over-bounce tests cannot distinguish the find/SELECT filters from sibling guards
evidence:
+  // A7: the cadence SELECT never returns a taken-over row, even when the
+  // clock is due.
+  let assert Ok(returned) =
+    rc_sql.sweep_due_reference_calls(db, "2099-01-01T00:00:00Z", 50)
+  // The employer row is still queued + due, so exactly ONE row comes back
+  // (the taken-over landlord row is excluded).
+  list.length(returned.rows) |> should.equal(1)
detail: Takeover NULLs next_attempt_at, so the due-SELECT excludes the row via the NULL clock even without the taken_over_at filter; the bounce test likewise passes on the mark_awaiting SQL backstop alone. The claimed find/SELECT exclusions are not isolated.
recommended_fix: After takeover, set next_attempt_at to a due value before asserting the SELECT excludes the row, and drop the fallback-match path from the bounce fixture so only the find filter can explain the stand-down.

title: The kind-tag consumer exclusion has no biting test — the co-nudge fixture is the untagged legacy shape
evidence:
+  // A corrected row whose attempts include a LEGACY (untagged) co-nudge
+  // entry — the single-email batch shape (no sms sibling at the same at),
+  // POST-correction: without the exclusion a bounce of the applicant's
+  // address would exhaust the row (r4 W1/W2 — the fixture BITES).
+  let assert Ok(_) =
+    pog.query(
+      "UPDATE reference_call
+       SET status = 'awaiting_correction'::reference_call_status,
+           attempts = jsonb_build_array(
+             jsonb_build_object('at', to_char(now() - interval '1 hour', 'YYYY-MM-DD\"T\"HH24:MI:SS\"Z\"'), 'channel', 'email', 'outcome', 'delivered', 'detail', 'ref_send_1'),
+             jsonb_build_object('at', to_char(now() + interval '30 seconds', 'YYYY-MM-DD\"T\"HH24:MI:SS\"Z\"'), 'channel', 'email', 'outcome', 'delivered', 'detail', 'co_nudge_send_1')
+           )
+       WHERE id = $1::uuid",
+    )
detail: The fixture's co-nudge entry is untagged email-only, caught by the email-without-sms clause — not the e ? 'kind' clause. A production-shaped kind-tagged co-nudge with an sms sibling would exhaust if the kind clause regressed, and no test would notice.
recommended_fix: Add a fixture with a kind-tagged co-nudge entry plus an sms sibling at the same at, and assert its bounce stands down via the kind exclusion.
